events.title: Saqifah and Abu Bakr's pledge
events.summary: Hours after the Prophet's death the Ansar gather at Saqifah Banu Sa'idah; Umar pledges to Abu Bakr and the community follows. His caliphate lasts about two years and three months.

steps.title: The shock of the death
steps.summary: Umar cannot believe the Prophet has died; Abu Bakr recites that Muhammad is only a messenger and that messengers passed before him, and the people take it as new.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: The meeting at Saqifah
steps.summary: The Ansar meet to choose a leader; Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubaydah go to them. Abu Bakr reminds them that leadership belongs to Quraysh and proposes Umar or Abu Ubaydah.

steps.title: Umar's pledge, then the people's
steps.summary: Umar takes Abu Bakr's hand and pledges first; the Ansar and then the whole community pledge, the general pledge following in the mosque. Umar later called the first pledge sudden but saved from harm.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Abu Bakr's first speech
steps.summary: He asks the people to help him if he does right and correct him if he errs, and says obedience is owed only while he obeys Allah and His Messenger.

steps.title: Usamah's army sent out
steps.summary: Abu Bakr sends the army the Prophet had readied under Usamah ibn Zayd toward Sham, refusing advice to hold it back. It returns victorious after about forty days.

events.title: The wars of apostasy and zakah
events.summary: Many tribes leave Islam or withhold zakah. Abu Bakr fights them in the name of the whole religion, and the revolt ends at Yamamah.

steps.title: Tribes withhold zakah
steps.summary: Several tribes refuse to pay zakah to Madinah. Umar urges patience; Abu Bakr answers that he will fight whoever separates prayer from zakah.

steps.title: False prophets rise
steps.summary: Musaylimah in Yamamah, Tulayhah among Asad and Ghatafan, and al-Aswad al-Ansi in Yemen claim prophethood, as does the woman Sajah among Tamim.

steps.title: Eleven columns
steps.summary: Abu Bakr ties eleven banners to eleven commanders, among them Khalid ibn al-Walid, and sends them across Arabia. Tulayhah is beaten at Buzakhah.

steps.title: Yamamah
steps.summary: Khalid defeats the Banu Hanifah at Aqraba; Musaylimah is killed. Reports give a large number of Qur'an reciters among the Muslim dead.

events.title: The first collecting of the Qur'an
events.summary: After Yamamah, Umar urges Abu Bakr to gather the Qur'an in one place. Zayd ibn Thabit collects it from what was written and what was memorised.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Fear of loss
steps.summary: So many reciters had died at Yamamah that Umar feared parts of the Qur'an would go with them. Abu Bakr hesitated to do what the Prophet had not done, then accepted.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Zayd ibn Thabit is chosen
steps.summary: Zayd, a young scribe of the revelation, is told to search out the Qur'an. He later said moving a mountain would have been lighter than the task.

steps.title: Two witnesses for every verse
steps.summary: Zayd accepts a verse only if it is written and also confirmed by two people who heard it from the Prophet. The last verses of Surat al-Tawbah are found with Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari.

steps.title: The sheets are kept
steps.summary: The sheets stay with Abu Bakr, then Umar, then pass to Umar's daughter Hafsah, the Prophet's wife.

events.title: Abu Bakr names Umar and dies; Umar's accession
events.summary: Ill with a fever, Abu Bakr consults the senior companions, names Umar, and dies on 22 Jumada al-Akhirah 13 AH. Umar rules about ten years and six months.

steps.title: Consultation
steps.summary: Abu Bakr asks Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Uthman and others about Umar, and has the choice read to the people so they can accept or refuse it.

steps.title: Abu Bakr's death
steps.summary: He dies aged about sixty-three, as the Prophet had, and is buried beside him in the chamber of A'ishah.

steps.title: Commander of the Believers
steps.summary: Umar is first addressed as Amir al-Mu'minin, shorter than 'successor of the successor of the Messenger of Allah'.

steps.title: Length of the reign
steps.summary: Sources give about ten years and six months, ending with his death in Dhu al-Hijjah 23 AH.

events.title: The conquest of Sham and Yarmuk
events.summary: Armies sent under Abu Bakr and Umar take Syria from Byzantium; the decisive battle at the Yarmuk in Rajab 15 AH opens the whole region.

steps.title: Four armies to Sham
steps.summary: Abu Bakr sends Abu Ubaydah, Amr ibn al-As, Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan and Shurahbil ibn Hasanah toward Syria.

steps.title: Khalid arrives from Iraq
steps.summary: Khalid ibn al-Walid crosses the desert to Syria with a picked force and joins the armies; sources differ on the exact route and dates.

steps.title: The battle of Yarmuk
steps.summary: A Byzantine army much larger than the Muslim force is broken over several days. The date is Rajab 15 AH in most sources, though some give 13 or 14 AH.

steps.title: Damascus and the north
steps.summary: Damascus is taken by treaty and force after a siege, Hims and Qinnasrin follow, and Heraclius withdraws.

events.title: Qadisiyyah and Persia
events.summary: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeats the Persian army at Qadisiyyah; Ctesiphon falls, and Nahawand in 21 AH ends organised Persian resistance.

steps.title: The battle of Qadisiyyah
steps.summary: After days of fighting, the Persian commander Rustam is killed and his army scatters. Sources differ between 14 and 15 AH.

steps.title: Ctesiphon taken
steps.summary: The Muslims cross the Tigris and enter the Persian capital; the emperor Yazdegerd flees east.

steps.title: Kufa and Basra founded
steps.summary: Garrison cities are built so that the army does not settle among the farmland; Kufa is dated to 17 AH, Basra to about 14 to 16.

steps.title: Nahawand, the victory of victories
steps.summary: A large Persian force gathers at Nahawand and is defeated; the Muslims called it the victory of victories.

events.title: Jerusalem received by Umar
events.summary: The Christian patriarch Sophronius surrenders Jerusalem on terms and asks that the caliph receive it in person. Umar travels to Sham and gives a written guarantee of safety.

steps.title: Siege and terms
steps.summary: After a siege by Abu Ubaydah and Amr ibn al-As, the people ask for peace on condition that Umar himself comes.

steps.title: Umar's journey
steps.summary: He travels with a servant, and the stories of sharing the one mount with him are widely told.

steps.title: The covenant of Aelia
steps.summary: The people of Aelia are promised safety for their lives, churches and property; the exact text and its conditions are debated.

steps.title: Where he prayed
steps.summary: Umar is reported to have prayed outside the Church of the Holy Sepulchre so that it would not be taken as a mosque, and to have cleared the Temple Mount.

events.title: The Hijri calendar and the diwan
events.summary: Umar and the companions choose the Hijrah as year one and begin a register of stipends for the army and the community.

steps.title: A letter with no year
steps.summary: A governor, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, complains that Umar's letters carry only a month, which makes it hard to say which came first.

steps.title: The Hijrah chosen
steps.summary: Options such as the Prophet's birth, mission or death are weighed, and the Hijrah is chosen, with Muharram as the first month. Sources differ between 16 and 17 AH.

steps.title: The diwan
steps.summary: A register of names, ranked by early Islam and nearness to the Prophet, fixes each person's yearly stipend. Its date is also given as 15 or 20 AH.

events.title: The plague of Amwas and the year of ashes
events.summary: Famine in Arabia, then a plague in Syria, take many lives, among them leading companions. Umar turns back at the border of Sham.

steps.title: The year of ashes
steps.summary: Drought and hunger strike the Hijaz. Umar feeds the people from stores brought in from Sham and Egypt and shares their hardship.

steps.title: The plague in Sham
steps.summary: A plague spreads through the army and towns of Syria; Abu Ubaydah, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan and others die. Counts of the dead vary widely.

steps.title: Umar turns back
steps.summary: Umar is about to enter Sham when told of the plague; he turns back, citing what the Prophet taught about not entering or leaving a plague land.

steps.title: Amr takes the lead
steps.summary: Amr ibn al-As persuades the army to scatter to the hills, and the plague ends there; Mu'awiyah is soon governor of Damascus.

events.title: Egypt under Amr ibn al-As
events.summary: Amr ibn al-As leads a small force into Egypt, takes the fortress of Babylon, and later Alexandria. Fustat becomes the new garrison city.

steps.title: Amr enters Egypt
steps.summary: With Umar's reluctant permission he crosses at al-Arish with about four thousand men; Zubayr ibn al-Awwam later brings reinforcement.

steps.title: The fortress of Babylon
steps.summary: After a siege the fortress falls by treaty; the dating of the treaty varies across sources from 19 to 21 AH.

steps.title: Alexandria
steps.summary: The Byzantine garrison surrenders by agreement. Alexandria is later retaken briefly and again recovered.

steps.title: Fustat founded
steps.summary: Amr lays out the tent city of Fustat and builds the mosque that still bears his name.

events.title: Umar's martyrdom and the council of six
events.summary: A Persian slave, Abu Lu'lu'ah, stabs Umar at the dawn prayer. Umar dies three days later and leaves the choice of his successor to six men.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: The stabbing
steps.summary: Abu Lu'lu'ah (Firuz), the slave of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, stabs Umar several times during the dawn prayer and then kills himself.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Umar's last days
steps.summary: He asks that debts be paid, sends greetings to A'ishah to ask for burial beside the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and she gives her permission.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: The six named
steps.summary: Umar names Uthman, Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, the ones the Prophet died pleased with, to choose one among themselves.

steps.title: Burial
steps.summary: Suhayb leads the funeral prayer; Umar is buried beside the Prophet and Abu Bakr.

events.title: Uthman's pledge
events.summary: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf consults the people for three days and then pledges to Uthman. His caliphate lasts about twelve years.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy
sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Abd al-Rahman withdraws
steps.summary: Abd al-Rahman asks the others to leave the choice to him and gives up his own claim, then asks for the opinion of the men and women of Madinah.

steps.title: Ali and Uthman
steps.summary: He asks each of them whether he would act by the Book, the example of the Prophet and the two successors; Uthman says yes without condition, Ali adds his own judgement.

steps.title: The pledge
steps.summary: Abd al-Rahman pledges to Uthman, Ali follows, and the people pledge in the mosque. The year is given as 23 or 24 AH because it fell at the turn of the year.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Length of the reign
steps.summary: Sources give about twelve years, or eleven years and some months, up to Dhu al-Hijjah 35 AH.

events.title: Uthman's conquests
events.summary: Armies move west into Ifriqiyah, east into Khurasan, north to Armenia, and the first Muslim fleet takes Cyprus under Mu'awiyah.

steps.title: Ifriqiyah
steps.summary: Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh defeats the Byzantine governor Gregory at Sufetula; North Africa is reached, though not held.

steps.title: Cyprus and the first fleet
steps.summary: Mu'awiyah, governor of Sham, takes Cyprus by sea after asking Uthman's leave, with some companions, among them Ubadah ibn al-Samit.

steps.title: Armenia and Khurasan
steps.summary: Campaigns reach Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Persian provinces revolt and are retaken as far as Khurasan.

steps.title: The battle of the Masts
steps.summary: A Muslim fleet meets the Byzantine fleet off Lycia, commonly dated 34 AH; it is the first major naval battle.

events.title: The standard copy of the Qur'an
events.summary: Hudhayfah warns of differing recitations on the northern front. Uthman has Hafsah's sheets copied into standard volumes sent to the main cities.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Hudhayfah's warning
steps.summary: Back from Armenia and Azerbaijan, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman tells Uthman that soldiers from Sham and Iraq are arguing over the recitation.

steps.title: Hafsah's sheets
steps.summary: Uthman asks Hafsah for the sheets Abu Bakr had gathered and promises to return them.

steps.title: The committee
steps.summary: Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-As and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith copy the text, and Quraysh dialect decides where they differ.

refs.checked: sunnah.com numbering, read on the hadith-api copy

steps.title: Copies sent, others burned
steps.summary: A copy goes to each major city with a reciter; other personal sheets are burned to end disputes. Dating runs from 25 to 30 AH.

events.title: The unrest and siege of Uthman
events.summary: Complaints against governors grow and groups from Egypt, Kufa and Basra march on Madinah. Uthman is besieged for about forty days and killed on 18 Dhu al-Hijjah 35 AH.

steps.title: Grievances
steps.summary: Critics objected to the governors he appointed from his own clan, to the use of funds and to land grants; Uthman answered many charges in speeches and the sources record both sides.

steps.title: The delegations
steps.summary: Parties arrive from Egypt, Kufa and Basra. Their grievances are partly settled, and then a letter attributed to Uthman is produced which he denied writing.

steps.title: The siege and his refusal
steps.summary: Uthman forbids the companions to fight for him in order to avoid Muslim blood, and says he will not leave the city or step down.

steps.title: His martyrdom
steps.summary: A group enters his house and kills him while he reads the Qur'an; he is buried at night in Baqi' al-Gharqad.

events.title: Ali's pledge
events.summary: Days after Uthman's death the people of Madinah, with the leading companions, pledge to Ali. His caliphate lasts about four years and nine months.

steps.title: The pledge in Madinah
steps.summary: After some reluctance Ali accepts; the men of Madinah and others pledge. Reports differ about the pledge of Talhah and al-Zubayr, who later said they gave it under pressure and left for Makkah.

steps.title: Calls for Uthman's killers
steps.summary: A call to bring Uthman's killers to account grows; Ali holds that order has to return first.

steps.title: Moving to Kufa
steps.summary: Ali leaves Madinah for Iraq, and Kufa becomes the seat of his caliphate.

steps.title: Length of the reign
steps.summary: About four years and nine months, ending on 17 or 21 Ramadan 40 AH.

events.title: The battle of the Camel
events.summary: Talhah, al-Zubayr and A'ishah go to Basra to press for justice for Uthman. Both sides want to avoid war, but it breaks out in Jumada al-Akhirah 36 AH.

steps.title: To Basra
steps.summary: A'ishah, Talhah and al-Zubayr march to Basra to call for justice for Uthman's killers; Ali follows with an army from Madinah and Kufa.

steps.title: Talks on the eve
steps.summary: Envoys, among them al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr, bring the sides close to agreement.

steps.title: Fighting breaks out
steps.summary: Reports say those involved in Uthman's killing, fearing agreement, begin the fighting by night; Talhah and al-Zubayr are killed, and A'ishah's camel is the centre of the battle.

steps.title: After the battle
steps.summary: Ali treats the defeated with respect, buries the dead of both sides, and sends A'ishah back to Madinah with honour.

events.title: Siffin and the arbitration
events.summary: Ali and Mu'awiyah meet at Siffin on the Euphrates. When the fighting stops after Mu'awiyah's side raises copies of the Qur'an, the dispute goes to two arbiters.

steps.title: The armies meet
steps.summary: Mu'awiyah, governor of Sham, asks for Uthman's killers first; Ali asks for pledge first. The armies camp at Siffin.

steps.title: Ammar ibn Yasir killed
steps.summary: Ammar, who fights with Ali, dies in the battle; his death recalls the Prophet's words that a rebellious group would kill him.

steps.title: The copies raised
steps.summary: With Ali's side gaining ground, men in Mu'awiyah's army raise copies of the Qur'an on spears and call for judgement by it. Part of Ali's army insists on stopping.

steps.title: The two arbiters
steps.summary: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari for Ali and Amr ibn al-As for Mu'awiyah are named. The details of their meeting are told in different ways and the outcome settled nothing.

events.title: The Khawarij and Nahrawan
events.summary: Some who had fought for Ali break away over arbitration, saying judgement belongs to Allah alone. After they kill a companion and his family, Ali fights them at Nahrawan.

steps.title: The secession
steps.summary: Some thousands leave the army at Harura and settle apart from Ali, who debates them through Ibn Abbas, and many return.

steps.title: Abdullah ibn Khabbab killed
steps.summary: They kill Abdullah ibn Khabbab and slit open his pregnant wife; Ali demands the killers and they refuse.

steps.title: Nahrawan
steps.summary: Ali's army defeats them; nearly all of the Khawarij die. Their remnants and kin later raise revolts in Iraq.

steps.title: Sayings of the Prophet about them
steps.summary: Sources report Ali citing the Prophet's description of a people who recite but whose recitation does not pass their throats.

events.title: Ali's martyrdom
events.summary: Three Khawarij plan to kill Ali, Mu'awiyah and Amr ibn al-As; only Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam succeeds. Ali dies of the wound a few days later, on 21 Ramadan 40 AH.

steps.title: The conspiracy
steps.summary: Ibn Muljam, al-Burak ibn Abdullah and Amr ibn Bakr agree to kill three leaders on the same night; the other two attempts fail.

steps.title: The blow in Kufa
steps.summary: Ibn Muljam strikes Ali with a poisoned sword as he comes out for the dawn prayer.

steps.title: Last wishes
steps.summary: Ali tells his sons to keep taqwa, forbids mutilating Ibn Muljam, and says to strike only once in return.

steps.title: Death and burial
steps.summary: He dies at about sixty-three. The place of his grave is disputed. With his death the period of the four caliphs is complete.
